newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. renews mandate of Tajikistan observer group.
newsitem.headline: U.N. renews mandate of Tajikistan observer group.

text.p: The Security Council on Thursday unanimously approved a three-month extension, until September 15, of the 22-member U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT).
Tens of thousands of people have died and many more have lost their homes in a civil war that has devastated the former Soviet republic since it gained independence in 1991.

UNMOT works with a force of about 20,000 Russian-led troops deployed by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) serving as border guards and internal peacekeepers in the mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China. Tajik opposition fighters have operated out of camps in northern Afghanistan.

The Security Council resolution called on the government and United Tajik Opposition (UTO) to implement fully agreements reached in inter-Tajik talks and encouraged them to sign a general agreement on establishment of peace and national accord.
A signing ceremony is due to take place in Moscow June 27, attended by Tajikistan's President Imomali Rakhmonov and UTO leader Sayed Abdullo Nuri.
The resolution also called on the parties to cooperate further in ensuring the safety of U.N., CIS and other international personnel.
